title: Do the Motivational Factors of Artificial Intelligence Technology Influence Millennials more than Members of Generation Z in Online Transactions?
content: This study investigates artificial intelligence (AI) technology motivational factors that influence millennials and members of Generation Z in online transactions. These motivational factors shed light on which aspects of artificial intelligence technology ergonomics are acceptable to these consumer groups. This study examined the influence of these motivational factors of AI technology among millennials and members of Generation Z in online transactions. This study adopted a quantitative research method in gathering and analyzing its data. A total of 116 participants of Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC), Nigeria took part in this study. 47 of the participants were millennials, while 69 were members of Generation Z. Primary data was collected through a self-administered survey-questionnaire adopted from AIDUA and modified AIDUA, which included anthropomorphism, hedonic, utilitarian, and interaction convenience motivational factors of AI technology acceptance. This study utilized Statistical Package for Social Science (SPSS) version 26 in conducting the Mann-Whitney U-test for statistical analysis, while Gray and Kinnear's non-parametric effect size was used to interpret the practical significance of this study. The Mann-Whitney U-test showed that anthropomorphism, utilitarian, and interaction convenience motivational factors of AI technology acceptance significantly influenced millennials more than members of Generation Z in online transactions. Conversely, hedonic motivational factors of AI technology acceptance had a non-significant impact on millennials compared to members of Generation Z in online transactions. Arguably, the hedonic motivational factors of AI technology had a medium effect size difference between millennials and members of Generation Z in online transactions. However, anthropomorphism, utilitarian, and interaction convenience AI technology motivational factors had a small effect size among the two generational cohorts.
